title: Word Counter
story: You're pasting song lyrics into a document and wondering: how many words are in this verse? How many vowels hide in each line? Instead of counting by hand, you build two functions that analyze any text you throw at them.
why: Text analysis functions combine string iteration, character counting, and conditional logic — the same patterns used in search engines, spell checkers, and text editors.
analogy: Word counting and vowel counting are like two different scanners at airport security. The word scanner (`count_words`) looks for spaces — one type of delimiter. The vowel scanner (`count_vowels`) looks for specific letters — a completely different check. You don't build one scanner that does both; you build two specialized scanners, each excellent at its one job.
try_it: Analyze a longer song lyric or famous quote. Then add a `count_consonants(text: Str) -> Int` function that counts all alphabetic characters that aren't vowels. Verify that vowels + consonants equals total letters.
tips: Words = spaces + 1 works because spaces separate words — 'a b c' has 2 spaces, 3 words
Handle empty strings first: 0 characters means 0 words
Check both uppercase and lowercase vowels — 'A' and 'a' are different characters
Use `or` to chain multiple character comparisons in one condition
common_mistakes: Returning `spaces` instead of `spaces + 1` — a single word with no spaces returns 0 instead of 1
Forgetting to handle empty strings — str_len of '' is 0, returning 0+1=1 word incorrectly
Using `=` instead of `==` inside the character comparison condition
